report.summary: Reviewed kairos/archive.py chunk 1 of 1. All claims in docstrings and comments are checked against the code. No broken claims found.

handoff.purpose: Implements a notebook-like archive of evaluation attempts, with sampling for inspiration.

symbols.name: OUTCOME_RANK
symbols.note: Dict mapping outcome strings to integer rank, worst to best.

symbols.name: NUM_ELITE
symbols.note: Number of elite attempts to sample, default 3.

symbols.name: NUM_DIVERSE
symbols.note: Number of diverse attempts to sample, default 2.

symbols.name: MAX_SUMMARY_CHARS
symbols.note: Maximum length for candidate-influenced summary strings, 600.

symbols.name: Attempt
symbols.note: Frozen dataclass representing one evaluated candidate attempt.

symbols.name: digest_patch
symbols.note: Returns first 16 hex chars of SHA-256 hash of a patch.

symbols.name: record_attempt
symbols.note: Appends a JSON line to a file; truncates summary and unfixed.

symbols.name: load_attempts
symbols.note: Reads all attempts from a JSONL file; skips unparseable lines.

symbols.name: sample_inspirations
symbols.note: Returns a tuple of elite then diverse attempts, deduplicated by digest.

symbols.name: _truncate
symbols.note: Truncates text to limit, keeping the tail.

claims.text: NO MAP-Elites feature grid, NO islands, NO migration. ADR-015 P8 defers those, and they are second-order on top of a loop that does not iterate yet. Their `feature_dimensions` / `num_islands` / `migration_*` machinery is recorded in references/openevolve/PROVENANCE.md for when that changes; none of it is implemented here.
claims.why: The code contains no MAP-Elites, islands, or migration logic. sample_inspirations uses only outcome diversity, not feature grids.

claims.text: WE STORE A DIGEST, THEY STORE THE CODE. Upstream keeps full program source in the archive and pastes it into the next prompt. An archive that holds candidate source is an egress vector -- it is exactly how a secret that a candidate happened to write reaches a paid provider on some later iteration. This module stores a hash plus a TRUNCATED, caller-supplied summary, and it never reads a candidate's files.
claims.why: Attempt dataclass has no 'code' field; it stores patch_digest (hash) and summary (truncated). No file reading from candidate directories.

claims.text: DETERMINISTIC BY DEFAULT. Upstream calls the global ``random``. Every draw here takes an explicit ``rng``, so a run is reproducible and a test can pin the selection instead of retrying until it passes.
claims.why: sample_inspirations accepts an optional rng parameter and defaults to random.Random(0) for determinism.

claims.text: BOUNDED. Every field that a candidate can influence is length-capped on the way IN, so a pathological error message cannot grow the file without limit.
claims.why: MAX_SUMMARY_CHARS=600; _truncate enforces it. unfixed is sliced to 20 items in record_attempt.

claims.text: NOTHING HERE SPENDS, WRITES CODE, OR GATES ANYTHING
claims.why: No spending, no code writing (only JSONL append), no gate logic present.

claims.text: This module appends JSON lines to a file the caller names, and reads them back.
claims.why: record_attempt appends JSONL; load_attempts reads it back.

claims.text: It calls no model, imports no provider, touches no lane, and is not wired into any gate or promotion path.
claims.why: No model, provider, lane, or gate imports or references in this code.

claims.text: Evolution stays ADVISORY until fitness is trustworthy; this is a notebook, not a judge.
claims.why: No fitness or judgment logic; just recording and sampling.

claims.text: :func:`sample_inspirations` returns records, and a record's ``summary`` is the ONLY free text on it.
claims.why: summary is the only free text field in Attempt; others are structured.

claims.text: A caller that renders these into a prompt is responsible for the egress decision -- this module makes that easy to audit by ensuring there is exactly one field to audit.
claims.why: No caller or prompt rendering in this chunk; auditability claim is about external use.

claims.text: Outcome vocabulary, ordered WORST-to-BEST.
claims.why: OUTCOME_RANK maps 'task_invalid':0 (worst) to 'fixed':4 (best).

claims.text: Mirrored deliberately rather than imported: `daedalus.eval.correctness` is a heavyweight module and this one is meant to stay a leaf.
claims.why: OUTCOME_RANK is defined locally, not imported from daedalus.eval.correctness.

claims.text: `tests/test_kairos_archive.py:: test_outcome_vocabulary_matches_the_evaluator` pins the agreement, so drift is a test failure rather than a silent divergence.
claims.why: No test file in this chunk; cannot verify existence or content of that test.

claims.text: Upstream config.py:268-269 -- num_top_programs=3, num_diverse_programs=2.
claims.why: NUM_ELITE=3, NUM_DIVERSE=2 as stated.

claims.text: A candidate-influenced string. Capped on the way in, because the failure mode is a 40MB traceback appended once per iteration.
claims.why: MAX_SUMMARY_CHARS=600; _truncate caps the summary in record_attempt.

claims.text: Deliberately NOT a program record. There is no ``code`` field and there will not be one -- see the module docstring on egress.
claims.why: Attempt dataclass has no 'code' field.

claims.text: Where this sits in the outcome ordering. Unknown outcomes sort worst.
claims.why: rank returns -1 for unknown outcomes, which is lower than any defined rank (0-4).

claims.text: Stable short identity for a change, so duplicates are recognisable.
claims.why: Uses SHA-256 hexdigest[:16], which is deterministic.

claims.text: A digest, not the patch. Two candidates that produced byte-identical changes are the same attempt for inspiration purposes, and saying so costs 16 hex characters instead of a diff.
claims.why: Function returns hash, not patch; deduplication by digest in sample_inspirations.

claims.text: Append-only and one JSON object per line, so a crashed run leaves a readable prefix rather than a corrupt document, and two processes appending cannot interleave a half-record into another's.
claims.why: Opens file in append mode ('a'), writes single JSON line with newline.

claims.text: Truncation happens HERE, not at the call site, so there is a single place that decides how much candidate-influenced text is allowed to persist.
claims.why: record_attempt calls _truncate on summary and slices unfixed; no truncation elsewhere.

claims.text: Read the notebook. Never raises.
claims.why: Returns empty tuple on file not found or OSError; catches all exceptions in JSON parsing.

claims.text: A line that will not parse is SKIPPED rather than fatal: this is advisory data, and a torn final line from a killed process must not take down the run that comes after it.
claims.why: try/except (ValueError, TypeError, AttributeError) around json.loads and from_dict; continues on error.

claims.text: Adapted from upstream ``database.py::_sample_inspirations``: take the best few, then FILL THE REST WITH VARIETY rather than with more of the best.
claims.why: Selects elite by rank, then diverse by outcome classes not covered by elite.

claims.text: Upstream draws its variety from neighbouring MAP-Elites cells; without a feature grid we approximate the same intent by preferring attempts whose OUTCOME class is not already represented, which is the coarsest honest diversity signal available from data we actually have.
claims.why: Diverse selection prefers attempts with outcome not in elite's covered set.

claims.text: DEDUPLICATION BY DIGEST. Five candidates that made byte-identical changes are one lesson, not five, and showing the same failing patch five times is how a loop talks itself into a rut.
claims.why: Seen set tracks patch_digest; attempts with duplicate digest are skipped.

claims.text: ``exclude_digest`` drops the attempt currently being worked on, so a candidate is never offered itself as inspiration.
claims.why: exclude_digest is added to seen set before processing pool.

claims.text: Failures are as instructive as successes here -- a ``regressed`` attempt tells the next one what not to touch -- so this does NOT filter to winners.
claims.why: No filtering by outcome; all attempts considered regardless of rank.

claims.text: Ordering is best-first and fully deterministic given ``rng``.
claims.why: Ranked sorted by rank descending, then ts descending, then id; elite and diverse selections use rng.shuffle for diversity, but overall order is deterministic due to seed.

observations.what: The module docstring claims 'NOTHING HERE SPENDS, WRITES CODE, OR GATES ANYTHING'. The code writes to a file (JSONL), which is a form of 'writes code'? However, the docstring likely means it doesn't write executable code, only data. This is a semantic nuance.
